contract: Pure tenant lifecycle (none, provisioned, active, suspended, closing, erased) and one-use invitations over the "lifecycle", "invitations" and "switches" fields of the tenant control resource of domain/kill-switch. prepare/3 is an assembly/checked-command preparer for payload {op, ...} with op provision, activate, suspend, close, erase, invite, accept or revoke and an exact facts record per command (now in Unix seconds 0..9_223_372_036_854_775; vault_erased for erase; code_digest, known_target and inviter_may_grant for invite; presented_digest for accept); it returns 1..3 writes on request.resource and writes the reserved lifecycle tenant switch through Elzoo.KillSwitch.engage/2 and release/2 (engaged_at now * 1000) in the same append: provision and suspend engage it, activate releases only it, close keeps or engages it and removes every pending invitation, erase keeps it and needs vault_erased true; erased is terminal. invite (active only) stores {code_digest, expires_at, id, invitee, issued_by, role, space} in 0..32 entries sorted by ID; accept (active only) removes the invitation and answers the six-key domain/membership record; revoke removes one. Refusals in the order invalid_request, terminal, invalid_transition, not_active, not_erased, not_permitted, then duplicate / too_many / unknown_invitation / expired / bad_code (:crypto.hash_equals/2) / wrong_invitee. gate/1 is the lifecycle descriptor gate over one resource/3 read: it allows the five lifecycle ops without Elzoo.KillSwitch.check/2 and calls check/2 for every other op. status/1 returns {:ok, state} or {:error, :unavailable}. No I/O, clock, process, storage, telemetry or log.
limits: The host vouches for the actor, the inviter's rights (inviter_may_grant), the existence of the space and role (known_target), erasure completion (vault_erased after state/retention-erasure reported every subject erased) and the time now.
A code's secrecy is the host's: an unkeyed SHA-256 digest is enough only for a high-entropy random code of at least 128 bits, which the host makes, sends out of band and never puts in a command.

No membership store: the host applies the accept response or the descriptor's outbox notice at most once per command identity. No reminder, resend or expiry sweep: an expired invitation stays until revoked or until close.

A command answered ASK is prepared again at release with the facts retained at proposal, so its now (and an accept's expiry check) is the proposal time; ASK is meant for lifecycle ops, and the Approval evidence age and expiry bound the delay.

Single use rests on removal plus CheckedCommand revision fencing: two accepts at one revision commit at most once and the other is retained as stale. A gate denial is retained under its operation ID, so a command refused while a switch was engaged needs a new operation_id after the release.

While any tenant switch is engaged (the lifecycle one included, so in provisioned, suspended and closing), the gate refuses invite, accept and revoke; close still removes every pending invitation. activate releases only the lifecycle switch, never an operator's switch of another reason.

A lifecycle command that would engage the lifecycle switch on a list of 64 other switches is refused too_many. The tenant, resource, actor, IDs, spaces, roles and invitees follow the domain/principal text rule, stricter than CheckedCommand identity: a nonconforming value is refused invalid_request, failing closed.

Selected Cure laws cover the transition table over the state and command Elixir decodes; shape validation, the facts checks, the invitation refusals, the switch writes and the gate are Elixir-side and test-grounded only.

grounding.claim: For every command, decide from erased gives TlTerminal.
provision from none moves to provisioned and engages the lifecycle switch.
activate from provisioned moves to active and releases the lifecycle switch.
activate from suspended moves to active and releases the lifecycle switch.
suspend from active moves to suspended and engages the lifecycle switch.
close from active moves to closing and engages the lifecycle switch.
close from suspended moves to closing with the lifecycle switch engaged.
erase from closing moves to erased and keeps the lifecycle switch.
Pinned Cure checks types and totality of the transition decision; the source audit reports no axiom, hole, unresolved, unaudited, opaque or unproved-total definition.

Listed scenarios: every listed transition and its lifecycle switch write with engaged_at now * 1000; every other (state, lifecycle op) pair invalid_transition or terminal, enumerated; invite and accept not_active or terminal outside active; not_erased for vault_erased false, nil, 1 and other values; check/2 deny after provision, suspend and close and allow after activate; an incident switch surviving activate; too_many on a full switch list; invite and accept with the exact stored record and six-key membership response; accept refusals in order (expired before bad_code, bad_code before wrong_invitee); expires_at == now expired and now + 1 passing; duplicate, too_many at the 33rd, not_permitted; close removing every invitation; revoke then accept unknown_invitation; no code bytes in any request, write or response; payloads with missing, extra or wrong-typed keys, texts at 0, 1, 128 and 129 bytes, invalid UTF-8, NUL, DEL and U+0085, digests of 31 and 33 bytes, times at -1 and one above the range, stored fields unsorted, duplicate, oversized or with an unknown state as invalid_request; status/1 over resource/3 results; on the Memory Store with real CheckedCommand descriptors, provision, activate, invite and accept commit, accept replay returns the first result, a second accept with a new ID is unknown_invitation, two accepts at one revision commit once with the other retained stale, a digest mismatch commits nothing, ASK for suspend unchanged until a distinct reviewer's once-evidence, activate through the lifecycle gate on a suspended tenant, invite, accept and revoke denied {:gate, tenant_suspended} under an incident switch with the invitation pending, the gate over PatternStep frames, and the accept response accepted by Elzoo.Membership.permissions/4. Keeping an accepted invitation pending, skipping the expiry check, letting activate release every tenant switch, allowing erase without vault_erased and skipping check/2 in the gate for accept each make these tests fail (negative controls). Finite scenarios, not universal proofs.
Pinned Cure compilation, reduction checking and BEAM decision semantics; compiler soundness not locally proved.
Pinned Elixir/OTP binary term order, List.keysort/2, String.valid?/1 and the utf8 binary pattern for the canonical invitation list and the text rule.
OTP 29.1.2 :crypto.hash_equals/2 compares the stored and presented digests; its constant-time property is the upstream contract, not locally measured.

The host authenticates actors and reviewers, resolves inviter rights and target existence, reports erasure completion, supplies the time, makes and sends high-entropy codes out of band, builds a lifecycle handle with gate/1 over a fresh resource/3 read before each command, owns the policy, Approval verifier and exact-value authority for the writes, and applies each accepted membership at most once.

telemetry.contract: Pure functions emit no observations and no logs; the host owns instrumentation.

config.contract: Fixed Contract bounds (32 invitations, 128-byte texts, 32-byte digests, 0..9_223_372_036_854_775 s); the read, request and facts are per-call operands, not settings.

control.contract: Lifecycle and invitation commands are retained, revision-fenced CheckedCommand commands through the host's descriptor with this preparer and gate/1; an ASK policy gives dual control through workflow/approval. No process or lifecycle of its own.
